prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B020 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The chain from proglucagon processing and human incretin physiology, through the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, to receptor biology and a drug class with randomized outcome-trial benefit in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease is original, mechanistically complete and independently confirmed for well over a decade. Round 1 did not weaken this case; it sharpened what the prize is for. All six of us converged on a discovery-centred configuration, and I agree with Sandberg that this should be a stated choice and not something reached by default through the three-name cap. I also agree with the chair that unanimity is not evidence and that the remaining work is on attribution and wording. I would therefore word the citation so that it honours the physiology and the identification of the active form, and says that these enabled the therapies, without claiming that the prize rewards the drugs themselves.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakest point. Habener, outside the credited names, has a priority claim on the active peptide that the supplied record does not settle in either direction, and Knudsen's long-acting analogues are what turned the physiology into a medicine; leaving her out is a real cost and a reasoned judgment, not a neutral one. If a majority concludes that the achievement is the therapy and not the hormone system, my trio is the wrong one, and the replacement would be Knudsen for Mojsov or Drucker, which I could not make without a clear stated reason. A single-part prize also gives up the chance to recognise a second achievement of high merit, and I have to admit that this is a loss for the committee even though the name cap makes the alternative costly.

responses.point: Sandberg moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to the Mojsov trio, but still doubts that a single-achievement prize is the best use of the committee's range and sees B045 and B040 as strong enough for a shared prize.
responses.response: I agree with your reasoning on the trio and with your point that a therapy-centred choice should be made openly. I disagree on adding a second part. The three-person cap means a two-part prize requires cutting one of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov, and each covers a distinct step that cannot be replaced: physiology, the active peptide, and the receptor biology and translation. Dropping any of them to make room weakens the strongest case on the list. Neither B045 (six credited names, early clinical translation) nor B040 (Eshhar outside the list) currently has an allocation I could defend as clean enough to justify that cost. So I would not take the shared prize unless someone can show a two-name allocation for the second part that survives the objections we both raised.

responses.point: As chair and in round 1, Svenningsson states a fallback in which the therapy, including long-acting analogues, is the achievement, and also raises long-term safety and durability of the obesity indication, which the chair's summary lists as an open question.
responses.response: On framing, I would accept your fallback only if the committee decides explicitly that the achievement is the therapy, and then the honest trio would be different from the one we are all proposing. I do not think the evidence pushes us there, because the target and the active molecule had to be defined before any analogue could be designed. On safety and durability, I take the point but would not let it change the timing or the wording much. Randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease cover several years of exposure and consistent benefit, and a citation about the discovery of the hormone system and its active form does not claim anything about lifelong safety. I would keep the wording tied to the discovery and its enabling role, which is the part that is settled, and leave the long-term profile out of the citation. Your remark about not relitigating attribution beyond what the evidence can settle is one I share.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius keeps B034 (TNF blockade) as her first fallback because its attribution is clean, while recognising that the work relies on antibody engineering and TNF biology by others and that her field proximity should be recorded.
responses.response: I take the cleanliness of the Feldmann and Maini pairing seriously, and it is cleaner than B040 or B045. I still would not place it in my alternatives ahead of them, for the reason you gave yourself: the contribution reads more as proof that blocking one cytokine treats disease than as a new discovery, and recognition of the cytokine-targeting field has already been extensive. What would move me up on B034 is evidence that the specific insight about TNF being dominant upstream in the synovium was decisive and not shared with groups outside the pair. I do not see that in the supplied record. I also note your disclosure of field proximity and see no need for recusal on that basis alone. It would matter only if B034 advanced.

responses.point: El-Manira describes optogenetics (B045) as a major method whose six-way credit cannot be reduced to three without leaving out someone with a strong claim, and says that if the achievement is the therapy rather than the hormone, his configuration is wrong.
responses.response: I agree that no trio of the six credited names is clean, which is why I keep B045 as an alternative and not as a second part. I would add that my own proposal (Deisseroth, Nagel, Hegemann) omits Boyden and Bamberg, so I cannot claim my split is the right one, and your trio omits Hegemann, whose characterisation of channelrhodopsin I still think is decisive. On your conditional about the therapy, I accept the logic but not the premise: I think the hormone-system discovery is the achievement, and your own words that drug engineering is a distinct and later contribution describe where I come out as well. If the committee decided otherwise, we would need a new discussion of the whole trio and not just a swap of one name.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks the unfolded protein response (B052) second as the most conceptually original candidate with the cleanest two-person attribution, but notes that its therapeutic payoff is still largely prospective and suggests it would fit as a companion part only if the name limit allowed it.
responses.response: I agree that Mori and Walter are the cleanest pair on the list and that the UPR is a prize-level discovery in basic cell biology. I do not think it competes with B020 now, and the name cap makes it a companion part only at the cost of a GLP-1 name, which I will not accept. I would put the question to you differently from the way the chair has: what would you accept as disease-relevant evidence from the UPR that is not just model-system inference? An approved drug is not required in my view, but human genetic or clinical evidence that the pathway drives a disease would change how I rank it. Without that I would hold it for a later year.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification of the active peptide stands against Habener's claim cannot be decided from the supplied record, so I rely on wording that credits identification of the active form without asserting sole priority.

Whether the committee honours the discovery or also the drug development is a judgment about the nature of the achievement, and a majority that chooses the therapy would change the trio to include Knudsen.
If a second part were pursued, I cannot identify one that has a clean allocation within the remaining name budget, and B040 would depend on whether Eshhar's absence can be defended.
Long-term safety and durability of the obesity indication are still accumulating, though I do not think this should change the wording or timing.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no documented involvement with any shortlisted candidate or credited name. My co-authorship of the 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper and eight co-authored works with Rickard Sandberg do not touch any shortlisted ballot. I note the disclosures by Wahren-Herlenius (B034 field proximity) and El-Manira (B045 broad field), and neither affects my view of B020.
